# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-10 13:01 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 179 active entries of tips_notebook.json (20 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier sheets are in history/.

## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit. A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone. (seen in 10 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results. Remember a contradiction alone doesn't separate a Yakuza from a Jester who wants the hang. (seen in 10 games)
- Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once. (seen in 9 games)
- Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information. (seen in 7 games)

## Village
- Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc. Require votes or a mechanical result before hanging on a PM link, since Jesters and Executioners also leave PM trails. (seen in 14 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, top suspects are those who voted No on their nomination, voted Innocent when it could have saved them, or PM'd them. A Guilty vote clears no one. (seen in 12 games)
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises far above awkward wording. Before a hang, ask what separates a lie from a mistake, a frame, a Roleplayer or a Jester. (seen in 12 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. While a Ritualist may live, never name a living player's exact role in public or in your will. (seen in 12 games)
- Keep Serial Killers and Arsonists in the pool after Yakuza die; a Not Evil read or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and a failed kill can mean innate Defense. (seen in 8 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. (seen in 8 games)
- Investigators and Medics: never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM; it tells the Pharmacist whom to block and the Katana where to strike. (seen in 6 games)
- Once an archive or survey list is public, do slot math daily; a claim that duplicates a once-listed role or overflows unseen slots marks a liar. (seen in 5 games)
- If an announced trial total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists among the voters on the larger side; pick them out by stance/ballot mismatch. (seen in 4 games)
- If the nominee may be a Jester, prefer not hanging; if you must, agree on a bare Guilty majority and keep confirmed power roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 4 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat: if your Innocents (plus a doubled vote) can save them, defend them. Futile lone Innocents hang you later. (seen in 15 games)
- Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict; never report more results than its tokens allow. (seen in 11 games)
- Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1; Eavesdroppers and Wiretaps read them, and PM triangles become the town's case. (seen in 10 games)
- After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 9 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with a cover story ready, and move it the same night a Lookout or Tracker names the holder. (seen in 7 games)
- Every member submits the agreed holder, target and actions every night; with two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 6 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit that could have been seen; agree a cover action in night chat and admit it at once. (seen in 5 games)
- Spend one-shot tokens (rig, puppet, clean) on a decisive day; a dead Yakuza's unused token is wasted. (seen in 4 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Sheriff
- Post every target and result in your first speech after getting it, and counterclaim at once with your full log if someone copies your role. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result clears nothing; say so when posting, and in the endgame rely on votes instead. (seen in 13 games)

## Medic
- Protect likely Katana targets, analysts then claimed investigators. Once you've claimed Medic, self-protect with a token instead of repeating a predictable protection. (seen in 11 games)
- You get no save feedback; say the target's survival is consistent with your protection, never that you confirmed a save. (seen in 4 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, Evil check against an unverifiable claim, flipped teammate's links), never a soft read; a hidden Cardinal costs two Good lives. Use Basic shots. (seen in 6 games)

## Clerk
- Rig on a set night for a non-teammate who can pass a nomination but not a Guilty vote; never when a teammate is the likely nominee, and don't hoard it. (seen in 4 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3+ living players are doused or the moment you're suspected; Arsonists who kept dousing were hanged with no kills. (seen in 3 games)

answers.confusing_rules: The Fortune Teller number rule (self-visits count, 'visited' counts once per player, visitors counts once per player) was hard to apply when a Lookout's watch was counted as a visit or not; the rules say Lookout watches are visits by the Lookout, which I initially misread. Add a small private group chat option for three players or a way to send a private message with a yes/no question. Show the remaining speaking budget and the trial-only budget more clearly in each prompt. Give the Yakuza a clearer summary of teammates' remaining tokens so swaps and rigs can be planned. answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to ask a single specific player a yes/no question in private and get a verifiable reply, but private replies are not sealed from the public record of who messaged whom. I wanted to write a note in my will as a live plan without it being an action. I also wanted a clean way to request a visit-denial be checked by a result, but no mechanism for checkable claims exists beyond the moderator's private results.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Several public messages were flagged as 'Guilty' in text but the revealed vote was Innocent, which the game treated as a legitimate wording slip; the game gave no way to correct a vote posted in text. The moderator's 'Fortune Teller numbers' results were unlabelled, which made claims about them impossible to verify without a visit log. The Day 5 private message from Grace to Dave was reported in the ledger only as a count, which is by design but made the 'Grace sent Dave a PM' suspicion hard to weigh. Some public posts were repeated verbatim across Days, which cluttered the record.
answers.suggestions: Publish a visit log (who visited whom) at the end of each night for players who are alive, or at least the count of visitors per player, so that Fortune Teller and Lookout claims can be tested. Add a requirement that a trial's Guilty/Innocent stance text must match the posted vote, or let players amend their vote. Show the remaining speaking budget and the price of the next message in the public ledger so players can plan. Clarify in the rules whether a Lookout's own visit to a player counts as a visit to that player in Fortune Teller totals.

Also unclear: whether a Lookout's watch on a player counts the watcher's own visit in the 'visitors' count the Fortune Teller sees (the game later confirmed it does, but I had to infer it). answers.missing_information: I needed a per-night visit list (who visited whom) for all players, not just my own watch results, to test Heidi's numbers. answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to ask a single player directly and privately whether they visited a named player on a named night and get a binding answer, but private messages carry no proof and the moderator never confirmed visits to watchers in a way I could use. I wanted to keep my Night 4 target private but also verify Dave's alert count; the Lookout watch on Dave confirmed one visitor but the moderator's report to me omitted the visitor's identity, so I could not test Heidi's counts directly.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Several inconsistencies: Judy's Night 4 result said 'You watched Dave. Nobody else visited Dave tonight' while Dave's own alert report said one player visited him and was killed, which is consistent only if that visitor was Judy herself; the message did not say so. Heidi's Night 3 numbers (3 and 3) gave a visit count that differed from the Night 3 Lookout result, which was hard to reconcile. answers.suggestions: Publish a per-night visit log (visitor to target) at the end of the game, or at least for dead players, so that Fortune Teller and Lookout claims can be checked. answers.confusing_rules: R8 says the Katana attack is dealt by whoever holds it and the holder may also use their own role action, but the night summaries show 'attacks None' or 'attacks Bob' without saying whether a Katana vote can name a holder who is not the sender. R19 says the Katana holder reads Good that night, which is easy to forget when reading Sheriff-style results. R9 and R20 do not say whether a role-blocked Katana holder still delivers the attack, so I was unsure. R13 allows wills at the start of each Day, but the summary never says whether a will update counts as a public action.
answers.missing_information: I never saw my remaining speaking budget or the price table in this game's history, so I could not judge how long to speak or whether a nomination was affordable. I could not see other players' visits except through summaries. Fortune Teller numbers arrive unlabelled, so the visit graph had to be rebuilt by hand each Day. These agree, but the wording of the public reveal ('Judy (Lookout, Veteran)') lists the cause as the Veteran role only, which is fine but easy to misread as a bug. Day 5 Dave's public message 'Carol, Erin, Mallory voted No on Erin's and Carol's nominations' appeared after the nomination was already settled, so the ordering of posts and votes in the log is hard to follow. Frank's Night 3 audit of Mallory gave 1 token, which I did not expect because I had spent none; I had no clerk token spend that night, so this was consistent, but the summary did not say whether tokens were counted at end of night after spends.
answers.suggestions: Show the remaining speaking budget and the price table in each turn's summary. Print the Katana holder and target in the Yakuza summary as explicit names rather than 'attacks None' or 'attacks Bob'. Put the visitor list in the Yakuza night report when a Fortune Teller or Lookout is alive, or at least state how many visits happened. Add a short public ledger line for each night's visit counts so players can test Fortune Teller numbers without reconstructing them. Make the ledger's trial vote lines include the nominator vote and the final tally in one line.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Medic protecting an alerted Veteran: the rules clearly make the Medic's visit trigger the Veteran's Strong Attack, and Standard protection doesn't stack with the alert's Standard Defense. I applied this as Alice dying with no special notice. I had to choose whether to tell her she 'gave Standard Defense' (R17 only forbids saying whether it stopped an attack), and I did. 2) R10/R20 don't say directly whether an investigator killed that night still gets their result. I gave Frank his N3 audit (Mallory, 1 token) along with his death notice. No rule says whether a will can be updated with a result learned the night you die. I assumed it can't (R13), so the result was lost to the town. 3) R6 versus player understanding: Heidi argued publicly that a Lookout watch isn't a visit. The rule is clear (it is a visit), but players clearly misread R6/R18. 4) The R16 day-end rule with the private-message 'last turn' exception was workable, but it's hard to state precisely when the day closes. 5) I had to decide how much each Yakuza summary names roles: Night 5 named 'Carol (Smuggler)', earlier nights didn't. R8 doesn't say whether Yakuza know each other's exact roles.
answers.missing_information: As moderator I had no automatic visit graph. I worked out the Fortune Teller numbers (N1 3/3, N2 3/4, N3 3/3), the Lookout results and the Veteran visitor counts by hand. They came out right, but it's error-prone. I also had no running token ledger (Dave 3→2→1→0, Bob 1→0, Mallory 1, Alice 2) and no RNG log for the Archivist draw (7 of 10, floor(0.75*10)). There was no stall-rule counter either, so I tracked the last death myself. Players found it hard to track who had publicly denied which visits, and to tie stated intentions to actual votes.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a structured, consistent template for night results. Phrasing drifted between nights: 'in no particular order' vs 'in no order', and the audit result was worded differently on N1 and N2. I also wanted a simple way to log interpretations, like the dead-investigator result, as public rulings. And I wanted a check that the night summary actually matched the recorded actions before sending it.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: 1) On Day 2 a '[Claim] Erin: Grunt (Village)' entry was published. This is Erin's true Yakuza role attached to a Village alignment. It looks like the claim tool defaulted to the player's real role, or let a player claim an enemy role with the wrong faction. It effectively outed her and drove the whole game. 2) Stated votes and cast votes didn't match far too often. On Erin's D3 trial, Grace (the nominator), Ivan and Judy all said Guilty but voted Innocent. On Grace's D3 trial, Ivan and Carol said Guilty and voted Innocent. On Grace's D6 trial, Carol said Guilty and voted Innocent. This smells like a confusing or flipped Guilty/Innocent interface rather than deliberate play, especially since it hurt both factions. 3) Repeated duplicate [Claim] entries (Dave's on Day 2) cluttered the log. 4) The Clerk and Smuggler never acted all game, which is fine, but Yakuza summaries kept saying 'no rig/no swap', which is redundant. No mechanical resolution errors that I could find: all deaths, counts and tokens check out.
answers.suggestions: 1) Validate claims: either block claiming a role with a mismatched faction, or make sure the claim field never pre-fills the true role. 2) After each trial vote, show each voter a confirmation ('You voted GUILTY on X'), or require an explicit confirm, to cut down the stated/cast mismatches. 3) Give the moderator built-in tools: a visit graph that auto-computes Fortune Teller, Lookout, Tracker, Cartographer and Veteran counts; a token ledger; a stall counter; and logged RNG draws. 4) Standardise result templates per role. 5) Add explicit rules for: results delivered to investigators who die that night; whether Yakuza know each other's exact roles; and a reminder in R6 that Lookout and Medic actions are visits. 6) Give each player a public list of who has denied or confirmed visits each night, so the town can reason over it without spending speech budget restating it.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Protect the player most likely to be a Katana target, but rotate who you protect so a Yakuza can't predict your protection; a self-protect costs a token, so keep one spare for a late-game duel.

Treat a Fortune Teller's unlabelled numbers as a constraint to test against known visit records, not as proof; the holder's visit set was ambiguous for several nights and the Village chased one suspect too long.

Before nominating or voting Guilty, ask whether the target's own claims and results contradict each other; behaviour patterns (late answers, pushing trials) are weak reasons to hang and cost the Village Vanillas.
Watch for a bloc that votes identically on every nomination for several Days; when three players march together, a concrete mismatch in one of them is the best lead to press.
Count the living Yakuza and the stall rule early: a Yakuza team that has lost its kill-capable members can only win by a kill on schedule, so track Katana holders and their visit sets nightly.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't hint at your power role on Day 1.
tips_feedback.why: Staying hidden kept me alive through Night 1 and Night 2, which mattered because my protection was the only defense against the Katana for a while.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target publicly or by PM.
tips_feedback.why: I kept my Night 2 protection plan private; Dave's alert and my protection were not signalled to the Yakuza in advance.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Several Day 3 and Day 6 hangings were debated on concrete mismatches, and the Village avoided hanging on pure pattern reads until the very end.

output.reason: Reviewing the game for reusable lessons and which tips were relevant to this game.

tips_feedback.tip: A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's 'Guilty on Grace' then Innocent mismatch was used to nominate her, and the Village spent Days 3 to 5 on wording that Carol then explained away, while her bloc kept voting together.

lessons.tip: Post your visit-count numbers with explicit visitor names as soon as they land and keep them consistent; unlabelled counts plus a Lookout watch left the table unable to pin the fourth visitor, and I died before the count could be tested.

Treat a single unexplained slip (like a wrong role claim) as weak; the Village hanged on behaviour reads (late answers, nominations) while the Yakuza bloc of Carol, Erin and Mallory voted identically from Day 5 and won by voting together.

When several Village players share a suspicion, split who nominates and who votes so a bloc cannot exploit a single trial; Ivan and Grace pushing trials on each other let the Yakuza bloc win the numbers.
Track who votes identically across every nomination; a three-player bloc that votes as one is itself the mechanical lead, and it should be named with the vote record early.

Visitor-count claims are only as strong as the counted visits; when a Veteran alert kill is publicly confirmed, the visitor list it produces is a hard fact that should anchor every count checked after it.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat.
tips_feedback.why: Several players (including me) had to correct claims about Veteran alert visits and Lookout watches being visits, and the rule-check kept Dave's alert account and Judy's watch from being dismissed.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Votes on Erin and Grace were held to the Grunt slip and the visit denials, which kept the Village from hanging on pure vibes early, though the Carol and Ivan mismatches were used by both sides.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's 'Guilty on Grace' posts followed by Innocent votes were exploited by Village players as a lead, and the Yakuza bloc turned the same kind of mismatch against Ivan and Grace, so the tip was used as a predictable weapon.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty; defend them when Innocents can save them.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza bloc of Carol, Erin and Mallory voted together on every nomination after Day 5 and used it to hang Ivan and nearly Grace, which is the pattern this tip describes.

lessons.tip: A mismatch the player has already explained once is not a fresh lead. Carol's Guilty-then-Innocent point was renominated three times across two Days, and my own renomination on it preceded my execution. Require a new fact before each renomination.

Name a bloc early when its members vote identically on every nomination and trial for a day or more, and ask each member the same concrete question in public. Carol, Erin and Mallory voted as one unit from Day 5 and won the endgame.

The Katana holder killed the Archivist, Accountant, Fortune Teller and Veteran by Night 5. Post results publicly as soon as they are safe, and give Fortune Teller counts with each visitor named, since an unnamed count could not be tested after she died.

Visit-count results (Fortune Teller numbers, Lookout watches) cannot name a Katana visitor. Use a count as a test only when each visitor is named, and do not nominate on a suspect list derived from a bare count.

One Katana holder who never moves the Katana, with teammates voting the same nightly target, was the trio's strongest engine. Aim each kill at whoever holds the most information, and let the holder stay low-profile in public.

tips_feedback.tip: Map early PM clusters and co-nominations; a group that DMs then pushes together is a likely bloc.
tips_feedback.why: Village players treated my two private messages to Grace as evidence of a bloc, and that PM link became part of the case that hanged me. PM trails are weak evidence on their own, as the tip's own caveat says.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: It made trial votes demand specific mismatches, which kept several Village players from hanging on the Grunt slip and on late visit answers. It also showed that the Yakuza bloc's Guilty posts had no results behind them.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action: tracks and watches can't tell protection from framing or a Katana hit.
tips_feedback.why: It kept Judy's Lookout watches and Heidi's counts from being read as confirmed actions, so the Village did not treat a watch as a denial of anyone's own visit.

tips_feedback.tip: Write each night's planned target and all results into your will, labelled as plans, so your death still yields information.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi's and Dave's wills carried their numbers and alert results after they died, which kept the Village's visit reasoning going when those players could no longer speak.

lessons.tip: A Lookout's watch only reveals visits to the watched player, so a clean watch on a Yakuza suspect rules out nothing about that suspect's own nightly visits; use watches on likely Katana targets or on players who claim to be Veteran-adjacent instead of on quiet players.

Check a Fortune Teller's numbers against visit records before building cases on them; the numbers only fit a visit set and several sets often fit, so treat them as a constraint on counts rather than names.
Vote on a single target every night with a clearly stated holder; repeated 'ready' confirmations in night chat cost nothing but reveal the team's pattern to any Eavesdropper or post-game reader.

A trial pushed by one player before facts are in invites a bloc response; if you nominate, state the specific mechanical result you need, since behaviour-only nominations lead to lynches of Village players.

Stated votes that contradict posted intent (e.g. 'I vote Guilty' then Innocent) are a readable tell; either vote as you say or explain the change before the reveal, because the town will use the mismatch as a lead.

tips_feedback.tip: A corroborated Lookout's lone other visitor to a victim is near-proof; don't let the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat acquit a repeat visitor.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi's count and Dave's alert kills gave a constrained visitor set that the town used to narrow the Katana holder to a short list, which guided votes.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any change before voting. A read/vote mismatch is a lead to check against claims and results, never a reason to hang or shoot alone.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's 'Guilty on Grace' then Innocent mismatch was the most persistent lead and was used to justify several nominations without any mechanical result.

tips_feedback.tip: Get the mechanics right before calling a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat, unless a full role census plus flips proves a role exists exactly once.
tips_feedback.why: Several claims were tested against the archive list and visit counts rather than assumed false, which kept the Village from misreading optional non-actions as denials.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction in claims, votes or mechanical results.
tips_feedback.why: Several Guilty votes (including on Ivan and Grace) rested on behaviour and private messages rather than a checkable contradiction, so the tip was not reliably followed by anyone, including me.

lessons.tip: Once the Katana holder is known and the Village has a visible Veteran or Fortune Teller, count visitors before picking a target: a Fortune Teller's two numbers can expose a Katana visit, so kill the Fortune Teller early rather than letting their count name your visits.

When a Village player asks a plain yes-or-no visit question, answer immediately and plainly, and avoid any answer that can be checked against a visit count later; a late or dodged answer became the main lead against our own teammate-adjacent players.

Keep your voting pattern on nominations varied, for example one Yakuza votes No on an early nomination of a teammate-adjacent Village player, otherwise a three-member bloc that votes identically every time is visible to everyone and draws a bloc accusation.

A Veteran's alert kills show exactly who visited them, so a Veteran's alert counts plus the Katana's kill list pin the holder's visits; compare each Katana victim's death against every visit claim before trusting any Fortune Teller number.

Do not nominate a player on a wording or typo slip that the player has already explained; the same slip repeated in later votes was used to justify a chain of nominations and lost the Village its last Vanilla players.

tips_feedback.tip: Bus a doomed teammate with Yes and Guilty. But first do the vote math in night chat.
tips_feedback.why: Our Yakuza team kept the Katana holder alive by never exposing a teammate, and we avoided a wasted Guilty vote on a low-value member.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed Katana, assume protection or innate Defense: kill or block the protector, or hang the survivor, rather than retrying blindly.
tips_feedback.why: We chose targets with fresh info (Frank the auditor, Heidi the Fortune Teller) rather than repeating the same visible route.

tips_feedback.tip: Never put team plans in daytime PMs and don't PM teammates on Day 1.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza coordinated only in the night chat, so the Village never received a PM triangle linking us.

tips_feedback.tip: Fake-claim only a role whose token count matches yours and that no living holder, Lookout or Tracker can contradict.
tips_feedback.why: Our Yakuza never made a public role claim, so the Village could not test one against tokens or visits.
